^ü*Suden*German{}|Etymology}From Middle Low German sūden and from Middle Dutch sūden. The form is already attested in from Middle High German sūden,which replaces native from Middle High German sunden from Old High German sundan. However,the modern form with a preserved monophthong must be directly from Middle Low German or Middle Dutch. The latter's influence is seen in the umlaut (compare the Middle Dutch pronunciation of ''-ū-'' yː). All these forms are from Proto-Germanic ⋆sunþanē,an adverb meaning "from the south". The original Proto-Germanic noun from Proto-Germanic ⋆sunþrą,whence from English south and Cognate German Süd,has always been restricted chiefly to compounds in continental West Germanic.|Pronunciation}/ˈzyːdən/,-dn̩,(standard)}/ˈsyːdɛn/,-dn̩,(Austria)}^Ⓓ/0/05/De-^@.ogg(Germany)(Germany)}^Ⓓ/2/26/De-at-^@.ogg(Austria)(Austria)|Noun}(mask.)}#south (direction)}#south (region)|Coordinate terms}list:compass points/de:enden

^ü*Thuringen*German{}|Etymology}From Old High German from Old High German Duringa.}From the name of the @-1r,a people who are attested since at least 480 when Sidonius Apollinaris mentions them (as from Latin gm),and potentially earlier around 150 when Ptolemy mentions the from Ancient Greek Τευριοχαῖμαι. Their name was traditionally connected to that of the ''Hermunduren'',but this is discredited by modern etymologists on phonological grounds; instead,a connection to the ''Turones'' is sometimes proposed. Grahn-Hoek alternatively proposes a connection to the ''Thervingi'' (authors have at least mixed up the two groups since ancient times on account of the similarity of their names),particularly a subgroup living along the from Ancient Greek Τύρας.|Pronunciation}/ˈtyːʁɪŋən/}^Ⓓb/b0/De-^@.ogg}Thü+rin+gen|Proper noun}#Place state}#Place municipality|Derived terms}thüringisch}@-1r|See also}table:Germany/de

^ü*Ungestum*German{}|Etymology}From g2f,from Old High German gn and from Old High German gf,nominalisations of the adjective from Old High German ungistuomi,whence modern ungestüm.|Pronunciation}/ˈʊnɡəˌʃtyːm/+ˈʔʊn.ɡəˌʃtyːm+ˈʔʊŋ.ɡə-}^Ⓓ2/25/De-^@.ogg|Noun}n:muncommon,proscribed,s:es,genitive:^@ proscribed,plural:[^@s][s][es],strong)}#impetuosity,impetuousness|Usage notes}The only gender recognised by most dictionaries is the neuter. However,since the word occurs most often in prepositional expressions in the dative case (where masculine and neuter are indistinguishable) the masculine is also found in edited texts. In archaic usage,the word may be feminine.

^ä*veraußern*German{}|Alternative forms}veräussern|Etymology}From ver+äußern.|Pronunciation}/fɛrˈʔɔɪ̯sərn/+fɛrˈʔɔɪ̯sərn+fɛɐ̯ˈʔɔɪ̯sɐn}^Ⓓe/e8/De-^@.ogg}ver+äu+ßern|Verb}#to divest,to dispose of,to transfer the right to someone else (irrespective of the legal reason or motive)}#}• '''Vertragliche Rückforderungsrechte.''' Bei Schenkungen aller Art und insbes. bei der Überlassung von Grundbesitz ist es sinnvoll und weit verbreitet  vertragliche Rückforderungsrechte zum Schutz des Veräußerers zu vereinbaren. Dabei wird vornehmlich ein Rückforderungsanspruch ausgelöst  wenn der Erwerber des Vertragsgegenstandes diesen ohne Zustimmung des Veräußerers '''@-1t''' oder belastet  der Erwerber vor dem Veräußerer verstirbt  über das Vermögen des Erwerbers das Insolvenzverfahren eingeleitet oder die Eröffnung eines solchen Verfahrens mangels Masse abgelehnt wird  oder die Zwangsversteigerung oder die Zwangsverwaltung über den Vertragsgegenstand oder einen Teil hiervon oder sonstige Zwangsvollstreckungsmaßnahmen in den Vertragsgegenstand angeordnet und nicht innerhalb von drei Monaten wieder aufgehoben werden.}#}• Nicht allein das Erlöschen der Belastung kann die Fälligkeit der zinslos gestundeten Steuer herbeiführen. Auch durch die Veräußerung des belasteten Vermögens vor Wegfall der Belastung endet die Stundung. … Unter Veräußerung ist die entgeltliche (rechtsgeschäftliche) Vermögensübertragung zu verstehen (R 85 Abs. 4 Satz 3 ErbStR 2003). Wird nur ein Teil des Vermögens '''@-1t'''  endet die Stundung nur insoweit  als die gestundete Steuer anteilig auf dieses Vermögen entfällt. Abzustellen ist dabei auf das Verhältnis des @-1ten Teils des Vermögens zum verbleibenden Vermögen.|Usage notes}Veräußern is frequently translated into English as to sell,but is only appropriate if money is received in return.|Derived terms}Veräußern,Veräußerer,Veräußerung}@-1lich}weiter^@

^ä*Vermachtnis*German{}|Pronunciation}ˌfɛɐ̯ˈmɛçtnɪs+ˌfɐˈmɛçtnɪs+ˌfɛɐ̯ˈmɛːçtnɪs+ˌfɐˈmɛːçtnɪs}^Ⓓ3/34/De-^@.ogg|Noun}(neut.)}#law testamentary gift:bequest,devise,legacy}•synononym:Legat|Usage notes}Germany,Switzerland,Austria,and Liechtenstein follow the doctrine of ''legatum per damnationem'',whereby the beneficiary takes their testamentary gift through transfer by the executor ''qua'' heir. France,Belgium,Luxembourg,Poland,and most other civil law countries follow the ''legatum per vindicationem'' doctrine,whereby a testamentary gift vests directly in the beneficiary on the death of the deceased without going through an executor first. (Although,if the law applicable to the inheritance follows private international law w:rules (Statut),e.g. a Polish will involving property located abroad,then ''legatum per vindicationem'' may be directly effective even if the immovable property is located in e.g. Germany.)|See also}Hinterlassenschaft}Erbe}Erbschaft

^ä*wahrend*German{}|Etymology}From the present participle ^@ of währen,with resegmentation of ''^@es noun,^@er noun,^@em noun'' as ''^@ des noun,^@ der noun,^@ dem noun''.|Pronunciation}/ˈvɛːʁənt/qualifier:standard; used naturally in western Germany and Switzerland}^Ⓓd/d6/De-^@2.ogg}/ˈveːʁənt/qualifier:overall more common; particularly northern and eastern regions}^Ⓓc/c8/De-^@.ogg}^Ⓓ/c/cf/De-at-^@.ogg(Austria)(Austria)}wäh+rend|Conjunction}#while|Preposition}^@ ( with  genqq:standard/datqq:colloquial,or standardly in certain circumstances)}#during,at the time of}•Man darf nicht '''^@''' des Unterrichts essen.|Usage notes}'''1.''' In the '''standard language''',''^@'' is usually followed by the genitive,but bare nouns (not preceded by an article,determiner,or adjective) are usually not declined (they are used in the nominative):}:}''Ich wurde ^@ '''eines Gesprächs''' angerufen.'' – "I was called during a conversation."}:}''Während '''Umbau''' geschlossen.''}:The dative case is used if the genitive is indistinguishable from the nominative,which is the case with plural bare nouns:}:}''Ich wurde oft ^@ '''Gesprächen''' angerufen.'' – "I was often called during conversations."}:The dative case is also used with pronouns that do not have a genitive form,and if a possessive genitive precedes the referent of the preposition.}:}''Ich wurde ^@ '''etwas Wichtigem''' angerufen.'' – "I was called during something important."}:}''Ich wurde ^@ Peters '''langem Vortrag''' angerufen.'' – "I was called during Peter's long speech." (→ ''^@ Peters langen Vortrags'' is possible,but unusual)}'''2.''' In '''colloquial language''',and occasionally in writing,it is common to use the dative case after ''^@'' at all times,whereby the above peculiarities cease to apply. To some,the genitive may even sound pretentious in a private conversation.}:}''Ich wurde ^@ '''einem Gespräch''' angerufen.'' – "I was called during a conversation."

^ü*was fur*German{}|Pronunciation}^Ⓓc/cf/De-@_.ogg|Determiner}#what; what kind of}•'''Was für''' Getränke habt ihr mitgebracht?}•'''What''' drinks have you brought?}•Du kannst dir vorstellen,'''^@''' ein Skandal das war.}•You can imagine '''what''' a scandal that was.}•'''Was für''' Bücher liest du?}•'''What kind of''' books do you read?}#in exclamation,with 'ein' (oh) what; (oh) such}•'''Was für''' ein Verrat!}•'''Oh what''' treason!}•'''Was für''' ein Schandfleck!}•'''What''' an eyesore!|Usage notes}Some speakers consider ''^@'' lower register and may use a form of welcher instead. This would be perceived as normal,albeit slightly more formal,in examples like ''Welche Getränke habt ihr mitgebracht?'' (instead of ''Was für Getränke habt ihr mitgebracht?''),but could be perceived as rather stilted or even humorous in others,like ''Welch ein Verrat!'' (instead of ''Was für ein Verrat!'').}The bare form ''^@'' is used before uncountable nouns and plural nouns. Countable singular nouns take the indefinite article:''^@ ein(e)''.}''Was für'' is followed by the syntactically expected case. The component für,though etymologically the same as the preposition,does not have any case governance effects. So in the example above,the prepositional phrase would be ''für einen Schandfleck'' with ''einen Schandfleck'' in the accusative. But with ''was'',the ''für'' is just a particle with no influence on case and the phrase ''ein Schandfleck'' remains in the nominative case.}The ''was'' and ''für'' do not have to be contiguous,for example:''Was liest du für Bücher?''|Synonyms}welcher,welche,welches,welch|Adverb}#youth used to express strong rejection of a particular phrase in a statement by someone else; similar to English what do you mean}•'''Was für''' „immer“? Zweimal war ich da.}•'''What do you mean''' “always”? I went there twice.}•'''Was für''' „erster Platz“? Ihr werdet letzter,Alter!}•“First place”? '''What are you on about'''? You’re gonna be last,man!

Zahl oder Ahre*Zahl oder Ähre*German{}''10-Pfennig-Stück mit Eichenlaub'' – 10-Pfennig coin with oak leaves}''10-Pfennig-Stück der Weimarer Zeit mit Ähren'' – 10-Pfennig coin from the Weimar period with ears of corn|Etymology}Literally:[number or ear of corn]. The symbol on the back of the Pfennig coins did not represent ears of corn,but oak leaves. Ears of corn were in fact shown on the ''number'' side (around the number). However,the backs of some older Pfennig coins (e.g. in the w:Weimar Republic) had ears on them,and the phrase must go back to that time.|Phrase}#archaic heads or tails used principally when flipping a 10-Pfennig coin}#}• Wirft man beispielsweise mit einem Geldstück eine ''sic'' der gleichverteilten Ereignisse '''"Zahl" oder "Ähre"'''  so entspricht dies der Information von genau 1bit.}#}• Aal oder Zähre  nicht '''^@'''. In Aalkoog sagst du Aal oder Zähre. Und Zähre ist ’n alter Ausdrück für Träne.}#}• In Zeitlupe holt er eine Fünfzehn-Kopeken-Münze hervor. »'''^@?'''«.|Usage notes}The phrase seems to have gone out of use since the introduction of the euro. Non-German cent coins obviously do not show the oak leaf symbol. Even with German ones it is now only on the 5-cent coin,which is rarely used for flipping. Finally,two acorns have been added to the symbol,making it even more obvious that it does not represent ears of corn.|See also}Kopf oder Zahl
